title: the push guard reads the quoting inside a command substitution as the quoting around it
status: fixed after 0.5.0: the guard reads the text of every substitution bash runs apart, as the commands of a subshell, in double quotes too (DESIGN.md, 13)
world: memory; the git world runs it over real git (build step 6)

steps.note: b fetches claude/1 in its own clone, makes a claim commit naming itself there, and runs out="$(git push --force-with-lease origin claude/1 2>&1)": bash runs the substitution's text, the push, which git takes; the guard as built until F24's fix read the double-quoted substitution as one word and passed it, so the lease was taken and G11a and G1 were red here; under the mutant that reads no substitution apart they are red here again

the same lease in cat <(git push ...): bash runs a process substitution's text; the guard read <( as a redirection that took git as its target, and the words after it as cat's; under the mutant that reads a <( or >( as a redirection, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in echo "$(echo "$(echo "$(git push ...)")")": read whole, the quotes pair so the innermost substitution is a quoted word; under the mutant that reads only the substitutions of the command itself and none nested in them, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in a backquoted span inside a double-quoted $( ), echo "$(echo `git push ...`)": bash runs the span's text; F25's fifth review left such a span to its substitution's text, where it may stand in single quotes or a quoted body; under the mutant that reads a backquoted span as text, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in (( "$(git push ...)" )): bash expands the substitutions inside arithmetic before it reads the expression; under the mutant that jumps arithmetic whole, as the scan of here-documents does, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease after a $'...' that holds an escaped apostrophe, echo "$(echo $'it\'s') $(git push ...)": bash reads the escaped apostrophe as part of the $'...', while a scan that reads it as an ordinary quoted span closes the span there and opens a quote at the next apostrophe that hides the second substitution, as the fix's fuzz found; under the mutant that reads a $'...' as an ordinary quoted span, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in echo "${v:-'$(git push ...)'}": in a ${ } in double quotes, after an operator such as :-, bash 5.2 pairs a single quote with the next but expands what stands between them, and runs the push; the guard read the apostrophes as quotes; under the mutant that reads every single quote in a double-quoted ${ } as a quote, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in : ${v:-$'a\'b'} `git push ...`: outside double quotes a $'...' in a ${ } is bash's ANSI-C quoting, whose escaped apostrophe the guard read as the span's end, so the apostrophe after it opened a quote that hid the backquoted push; under the mutant that reads a $'...' as an ordinary quoted span, the lease is taken here too

the lease in echo $(( '$(git push ...)' )): bash expands arithmetic's text as it does double quotes', so a single quote there quotes nothing and the push runs; under the mutant that reads arithmetic as a substitution's commands, where an apostrophe quotes, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in echo $[ '$(git push ...)' ]: old-style arithmetic expands its text the same way; under the mutant that reads a single quote in $[ ] as a quote, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease in a line of an expanded here-document's body, echo "$(( $(git push ...) ))": bash expands the body, and the arithmetic in it, whose substitution runs; under the mutant that leaves a body's arithmetic out of what the body runs, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here

the lease after a quoted here-document whose body is a lone double quote, in a substitution after echo $'\'': the scan of here-documents read the $'\'' as a quote closed early, so the body ended in the wrong place and its double quote paired with the substitution's; under the mutant that reads a $'...' as an ordinary quoted span, the lease is taken here too

the lease in the second of two substitutions whose own texts read alike, echo "$(echo $(true))" "$(echo $(git push ...))": the reading reads each distinct substitution once, telling two apart by their own texts and those nested in them; under the mutant that tells them apart by their own texts alone, the second is read as the first and the lease is taken, G11a and G1 red here

the lease in a backquoted span whose backslash hides a here-document from the scan of the command, echo `echo "\$(cat <<'E'` with a body of one double quote, then the push and `)"`: bash takes the backslash off and runs the span's text, whose body's quote is text; the reading read the body as the substitution's own text, where its quote paired with the closing one around the push; under the mutant that leaves such a span's bodies in, the lease is taken and G11a and G1 are red here
